title: 1.6 stops serving v1alpha2/v1alpha3/v1beta1 — unconverted manifests can no longer be applied

detection.reason: what breaks is manifests in Git, Helm charts and scripts that still use a legacy apiVersion, which are not cluster objects; every 1.5 CRD serves the legacy versions until the upgrade itself, so the served list cannot clear this either

quote: Following their deprecation in version 1.4, the cert-manager API versions `v1alpha2, v1alpha3, and v1beta1` are no longer served.
remediation: Convert every cert-manager manifest in Git, charts and scripts to `cert-manager.io/v1` (`cmctl convert`) before upgrading: from 1.6 the API server refuses the legacy versions, so a GitOps sync or `kubectl apply` of an unconverted manifest fails. On a cluster that ran cert-manager before v1.0, also run `cmctl upgrade migrate-api-version` so every CRD's storedVersions is `[v1]` (the command below).
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group | test("cert-manager\\.io$")) as $c | $c.status.storedVersions[] | select(. != "v1") | "\($c.metadata.name) still stores \(.)"'  # each row is a CRD still storing a legacy version (clusters that predate v1.0); NO rows = only your manifests need converting

title: v1.6.0 fails JKS keystore renewals with short passwords — install 1.6.1 or later

detection.reason: keystore passwords live in Secrets, which are never collected; and the patch version you will install is not a fact of the current cluster

quote: In cert-manager `v1.6.0` JKS Keystores had a minimum password length of 6 characters, as an unintended side effect of upgrading keystore-go from `v2` to `v4`. If you are using a shorter password, certificates would have failed to renew, and the only observable error was in the cert-manager logs. This was fixed in cert-manager `v1.6.1`.
remediation: Skip v1.6.0 and install the latest 1.6 patch.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("cert-manager")) | .spec.template.spec.containers[].image'  # lists, does not judge: a tag of v1.6.0 after the upgrade is the one release to avoid
